:::{#exr-direct-sum-practice}
#### Testing whether $\reals^3$ is the direct sum of a plane and a tilted line

The [direct sum](#def-direct-sum) $\mathcal{S}_1 \oplus \mathcal{S}_2$
needs the two [subspaces](linear-algebra-subspaces.qmd#def-subspace) to be [complementary](#def-complementary-subspaces).
Let $\mathcal{S}_1 = \cb{(a, b, 0) : a, b \in \reals}$, the plane $z = 0$,
and $\mathcal{S}_2 = \operatorname{span}\cb{(1, 1, 1)}$, a tilted line.

Decide whether $\reals^3 = \mathcal{S}_1 \oplus \mathcal{S}_2$.

::: {.callout-tip}
#### Hint

To write $(x, y, z)$ as a vector of $\mathcal{S}_1$ plus $c\,(1, 1, 1)$, the third entry fixes $c$.

:::
